beats.narration_en: This car just drifted into a concrete wall but only its tire ever touched it.
On a flat wall the same hit lands on the body, front corner first and then the rear.
A Jersey barrier is shaped differently because its lower face leans back like a steep ramp.
The tire meets that slope first and climbs it, squeezing the suspension and softening the hit.
The slope pushes back on the tire and steers the car toward its lane with the body untouched.
That is why this simple concrete shape lines highways and work zones all across America.
